interactions.prompt: "The determination (adhyavasāya) establishes an external object." Who is committed to this?

options.text: the Buddhist opponent
Abhinavagupta himself
an unresolved hypothetical reconstruction

interactions.feedback: This is the rival position the Śaiva is rejecting, not Abhinavagupta's own claim.

interactions.prompt: Which of these is Abhinavagupta's conclusion in the reflexion-core?

options.text: The cognition never establishes a thing outside itself.
The cognition reaches out to and establishes an external.
All consciousness is one single universal self.

interactions.feedback: The conclusion is that nothing is established outside self-luminous awareness; the universal-Self claim is explicitly NOT established here.

interactions.prompt: The conclusion (the determination establishes nothing external) depends on which premise?

options.text: An inert part cannot establish anything.
The trees on the far bank rush against the current.
Fire burns wood though inert.

interactions.feedback: 'Inertness blocks establishing' is the load-bearing premise; the fire-burning-wood line is the Buddhist's objection to it, not a Śaiva premise.

interactions.prompt: What warrants the step from 'the determination is inert/error-form' to 'nothing external is established'?

options.text: Establishing power belongs to self-luminous awareness (prakāśa), not to a thing that reaches a thing.
The passage simply asserts it, so no warrant is needed.
All external things are illusions.

interactions.feedback: The warrant is the self-luminosity of the establishing act — and the audit marks it as RECONSTRUCTED/UNRESOLVED, not a settled fact.

interactions.prompt: The Buddhist's 'as fire burns wood though inert' objection targets which Śaiva premise?

options.text: An inert thing cannot establish.
The determination is error-form.
Reflexivity is intrinsic to manifestation.

interactions.feedback: The fire analogy attacks the claim that inertness blocks establishing — it is the counterevidence (O3).

interactions.prompt: What is the smallest dispute on which the recognition conclusion turns?

options.text: Whether 'establishing' requires the self-luminous awareness itself, or an inert representation can establish.
Whether the text is by Abhinavagupta.
Whether Kālī is the supreme goddess.

interactions.feedback: The crux is the self-luminosity of the establishing act (CRUX-IPVV-001) — it stays OPEN, it is not settled.

interactions.prompt: The claim 'the external is only drawn-to by the impression, never established' is grounded in which?

options.text: the reflexion-core passage of the IPVV (chunkM)
the Buddhist's commentary
a modern textbook summary

interactions.feedback: The claim traces to the IPVV reflexion-core passage and the C1 interpretation — not to the rival or to a textbook.

interactions.prompt: Which reading is faithful? "The appearance is taken as external ..."

options.text: ... only for the slow-minded, in the illusion and the diseased-eye case.
... always and for everyone, since externality is universal.
... and therefore no distinction is ever drawn anywhere.

interactions.feedback: The source qualifies the outward-drawing as only for the slow-minded; the universal reading drops that qualification (QUALIFIER_DROP).
